To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HF thinking is relevant and applicable to contemporary management contexts.

(1) HF is a scientific discipline which has developed within high demand domains (aviation, medicine, military, infrastructure) to improve safety and performance, (2) the HF approach to safety is based on a systems view of safety and a human centred view of performance, and (3) the HF approach can be applied in the context of executive decision making within corporations and financial markets to improve performance.

(a) the HF concepts of situation awareness (SA) and human factors (HF), developed in the aviation and military domains, are applicable to executive decision making in the business domain, and (b) SA and HF are useful in management education.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of human factors and safety concepts to the management of corporations, and the development of a management education framework to incorporate these concepts.

the question of whether HF concepts may be usefully applied in the context of executive decision making, and whether this is feasible within the current state of the art in management education and practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HF and SA thinking is not yet fully integrated within the management domain, but that it should be.
HF and SA are not well developed within the context of executive management.
the application of HF within executive decision making contexts has been only lightly explored.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the application of HF thinking to executive decision making is a promising and fruitful research area, and that there are opportunities to develop new knowledge and techniques which can be applied to management practice.
the application of SA and HF within management education is a promising and worthwhile endeavour, but it is a work in progress.
HF thinking and practices have much to offer to management education, and to the practice of management.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CEO is a 'pilot of the corporation', and the corporation itself is an 'aircraft' which has a life cycle.
the application of HF concepts and techniques to management and executive decision making is not a trivial undertaking.
the application of HF to executive decision making is not just a 'nice idea' but is a potentially powerful way to enhance the safety of organisations, their employees and customers.
